frequency_question: How often do comprehensive energy permitting and infrastructure reform bills successfully clear all legislative veto points and become law within a single congressional session?
membership_rule: Includes major bipartisan or partisan-forced energy permitting reform packages introduced with leadership backing that explicitly targeted National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and interstate pipeline approvals. Excludes minor provisions bundled unnoticed into must-pass appropriations unless subject to major standalone floor debates.

cases.name: Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007

coverage_note: 6 major standalone or primary vehicle attempts identified; 2 enacted.
known_gaps: Smaller provisions occasionally hitch rides on National Defense Authorization Acts (NDAA) or debt ceiling deals, which have a higher passage rate but represent narrow tweaks rather than comprehensive reform.
skeleton: Total major omnibus energy permitting reform legislative pushes identified across 15 two-year congressional sessions since 1995.
multiplier: 2 successful legislative outcomes out of 6 major targeted omnibus attempts where permitting reform was the core explicit vehicle.
validity_reason: The institutional filibuster rules and polarization dynamics governing these structural veto points remain stable across multiple recent Congresses.
